 Giannis Antetokounmpo with Bucks coach Doc Rivers when the two were on the same side, before a game against the Brooklyn Nets at Fiserv Forum on April 10, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) 
 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: November 12, 2026 at 6:05 AM EST | UPDATED: November 12, 2026 at 9:04 AM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Q: Ira, good job by Giannis Antetokounmpo showing Doc Rivers how to be diplomatic. I hope this whole thing blows over now, because the Heat never needed this distraction. — Cooper. 
 A: Except with Doc Rivers going from last season‘s role as Bucks coach to this season‘s role as an NBC analyst, there very much remains the chance that the two will cross paths this season. Speaking with Giannis , it is clear his belief remains that what happens in the locker room stays in the locker room. Apparently, Doc Rivers holds a different perspective. The bottom line is that Doc Rivers’ most critical comments about Giannis remain available for all to hear on a podcast, while his apology merely was passed along through an ESPN intermediary. On Tuesday night in Utah, whether Giannis actually saw a text from Doc Rivers, or not, it was clear he had greater concerns on his mind, including finally getting off the road.

 Q: Anyone else concerned it took a buzzer beater to beat a one-win Clippers team, a dogfight battle vs. the one-win Kings and a close win vs. the one-win Jazz with no Keyonte George or Lauri Markkanen? I’m very panicked. – Todd. 
 A: All reasonable and concerning points. But the converse could be looking at the six losses and saying other than the loss in Charlotte, which came in overtime, there really wasn’t a bad loss, with Minnesota, Detroit, Dallas, Lakers and Warriors all off to solid starts. And that run of quality opposition continues during the impending homestand, against the Cavaliers, Pistons, Rockets and Thunder. So you take what you can get against the bottom, hopefully build confidence, and then go from there.
 Q: Unless the Heat figure out their rotations and get some of the bench guys going, the starters will be worn out by midseason. They are playing an awful lot of minutes. – Rich, Plantation. 
 A: Which is why it would have been nice, as cited above, if the Heat could have taken care of business more efficiently against the Clippers, Kings and Jazz. But even in those games, Erik Spoelstra turned to alternatives, with Ryan Conwell, Myron Gardner and Simone Fontecchio getting opportunities. So there are other options to choose from, even if it is not the options originally anticipated, such as Tim Hardaway Jr. and Nikola Jovic.
